title: See the Harvest Moon Rise with Saturn This Weekend!
summary:
Get ready for a sky show! This weekend, the Harvest Moon — the first full moon of autumn — will rise in the eastern sky. And it's bringing a friend: Saturn, the ringed planet.

The Harvest Moon is famous because it's the full moon closest to the September equinox, which was on Sept. 22. Around this time, the moon rises only about 25 minutes later each night instead of the usual 50. That means several evenings in a row have bright moonlight soon after sunset. Long ago, farmers used this extra light to harvest crops. That's how it got its name.

This year, the Harvest Moon also happens during the Mid-Autumn Festival, celebrated in Chinese and Vietnamese communities.

On Saturday, Sept. 26, the moon will be officially full at 12:49 p.m. EDT. But the best time to see it is at moonrise, when it climbs above the eastern horizon. It will be in the constellation Pisces. Saturn will shine just below it. You can see both without a telescope, but binoculars will give you a crisper view.

Find a spot with a clear view to the east. The next full moon, the Hunter's Moon, will be a supermoon on Oct. 25 or 26. Don't miss this one!
why_it_matters: It is a free show you can share with your family — just step outside after dinner and look east, no telescope or ticket needed.

background_read: The Harvest Moon is the full moon closest to the September equinox (the day in early autumn when day and night are about the same length).
The Mid-Autumn Festival is a happy holiday celebrated in Chinese and Vietnamese communities, when families eat mooncakes and look at the full moon together.
Saturn (the sixth planet from the Sun, famous for its wide, bright rings) looks like a steady golden dot you can spot without any telescope.
Article_Structure: WHO: Sky watchers, farmers from long ago, and families celebrating the Mid-Autumn Festival.
WHAT: The Harvest Moon, the first full moon of autumn, rises in the sky with the planet Saturn shining just below it.
WHERE: In the eastern sky, in the constellation Pisces, best seen from a spot with a clear view to the east.
WHY: The extra evening moonlight helped farmers harvest crops long ago, and today it is a free sky show anyone can enjoy.

perspectives.description: They love that the moon and Saturn can be seen with just your eyes, so anyone can join in.
For them the Harvest Moon is a reminder of how farmers once used moonlight to keep working late in the fields.
Bright street lights and cloudy weather can hide Saturn, so they may have to travel to a darker spot to see it well.
